what: Ryanair is Europe's largest airline by passengers. It flies point-to-point short-haul routes across Europe with a single aircraft type, no frills included in the fare, and the lowest cost per passenger of any major airline in the world.
customers: European leisure and visiting-friends travellers, plus price-sensitive business travellers.
money: bags, seat selection, priority boarding, car hire and insurance
moat: A cost base roughly a third below its nearest competitors, built on one aircraft type, secondary airports, high aircraft utilisation and enormous bulk aircraft orders bought in downturns.
risks: Boeing delivery delays have limited how fast it can grow
Fuel prices move earnings and its hedging only delays the effect
European air traffic control strikes cause repeated disruption
Environmental taxes on flying are rising in several European countries
opportunities: Revenue grew about 13% last year and about 41% a year over three years
Cash of about $2.8 billion against very little debt, unusual for an airline
Weaker competitors retrenching leaves routes and airport slots for it to take
watch: Aircraft deliveries from Boeing and the average fare per passenger.
